notes:
Passed on the fake backend by `python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/daylily-informatics__zebra_day --backend fake`; the gate runs on 2026-11-17 printed digest sha256:c204145e2a8c2003ae6a4a51a14376b77517bcdfefade9c0e4cda0031dce248a and failed []; the --verbose run printed the same digest and the warnings recorded below. Evidence is contract_checked, not an MHS-Device level. No hardware, no network, and no upstream code was imported or run; the pinned clone stayed git-clean.

Covered: the selected entry `zebra_day.cmd_mgr:ZebraPrinter`. Reads are one status snapshot from `get_full_status` (host identification, serial, the raw error-status line, odometer, paused/paper_out/ribbon_out/head_up) and the raw `^HH` configuration report. The upstream wall-clock timestamp is removed from the served state so a read alone does not change the state hash. The one write is `set_configuration(configuration)`: the upstream raw ZPL configuration body followed by `^XA^JUS^XZ`. There is no numeric bound: no text of the clone or the cited manual states a bound for that string, so the driver does not invent one and ships no site-limits.example.json. The fake implements only the upstream public methods (send_command, get_configuration, set_configuration and the six other get_* methods); G7 passed.

NOT COVERED: label printing and print-job submission (`printer_protocol.send_zpl_code`, `client.print_label`). The card's entry symbol is ZebraPrinter, the status/config interface, and the card's hints.actions is empty; no catalogue class covers a print action. The raw configuration write can carry ZPL text, but the driver exposes no typed print action and makes no print confirmation. NOT COVERED: the upstream 60 s get_cached_status cache (reads are fresh), separate MHS fields for each get_* method (they are nested in status), and printhead/media maintenance. NOT COVERED: the other device classes and fleet/client layers of the repository.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper is PythonObjectDriver; this package is a decorated direct Driver (the card's decision is direct-driver). The stop has no upstream method: it sends the ZPL cancel-all frame `~JA` through `self.native.send_command`, which a config-only family table cannot express with a constant safety call. The upstream class is a plain Python object; no Serial/Scpi command table is involved. native.py is the hardware factory and imports the pinned `zebra_day.cmd_mgr:ZebraPrinter`; it was never run.

Safety: risk R2 because the thermal printhead is a heating element and the ZD620/ZD420 user guide warns of severe burns (PDF page 62). The independent stop is the front-panel POWER button held 4-9 s (PDF page 57), cited by estop_physical_ref; PAUSE/CANCEL are the print-job controls (PDF page 59). The upstream class has no stop, pause or cancel method. The @estop's `~JA` command is not documented in the clone or the cited PDF, so it is an unverified best-effort software cancel, not a sourced stop; a label already printing may finish and the print buffer is not cleared. The fake models `~JA` only as test data. There is no @reset hook; a reset only releases the latch. This package is model-authored and unreviewed: reviewed_by is null, and at R2 the loader refuses the hardware backend until a human signs it. No hardware run is claimed.

Fake fidelity: F0. The fake is an in-memory ZPL printer, not a recording and not the upstream simulator. Model, serial, firmware, counters and configuration frames are placeholders marked `# placeholder`. It reflects the last written configuration body in its next `^HH` report, a simulation assumption: a real `^HH` report may not show arbitrary raw ZPL commands. It returns a fixed status snapshot; no timing, media or printhead physics is modelled. The `cancelled` flag after `~JA` is test data.

Warnings: G4.REF_BINARY x4 (the four PDF citations: facts pages 57, 59 and 62 and estop_physical_ref page 57). The pages were read with a local PDF text extractor; the gate cannot read a PDF. G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE: the only actuator is the raw configuration string and no source states a bound, so there is no numeric out-of-limit input to probe; the suite awards CL2. There is no G4.REF_VALUE warning. No catalogue extension id was used, so no catalogue_requests entry is claimed.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-17; reviewed_by stays null): Model source review confirmed ZebraPrinter and R2 printhead hazards, but the pinned clone provides no acknowledged stop and raw configuration accepts arbitrary ZPL, including print commands. driver.py removes the undocumented ~JA stop and unsupported POWER-button emergency-stop reference, reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held, and reports configuration writes as unknown because cmd_mgr.py:47-54 discards the first result and send_command swallows transport failures. fake.py removes invented ~JA cancellation, test_driver.py adds failure-path regressions, and facts.md corrects POWER-button and write-outcome claims after a local model reading of PDF pages 57, 59 and 62. reference.json and REFERENCE.md were regenerated and check-report.json refreshed; all four package-specific cases pass, while the unchanged stock gate assertion fails G3/SAFE-045 because there is no independent stop or achieved safe state. The strict collector remains failing with RESULT_UNTRUSTED and three unsigned binary-citation warnings, which this model review does not waive. For the human reviewer: No upstream code, printer or network was run. The manual POWER-button table includes job-delayed sleep and power-failure recovery with automatic power-on (PDF page 57); PAUSE finishes the current label and can resume queued jobs, and CANCEL operates only while paused (page 59). Those controls do not prove an independent emergency stop for this binding. A returned configuration save reply cannot prove that the discarded first raw ZPL command succeeded; no automatic retry is justified. Before unblocking, provide a source-backed acknowledged stop and bounded typed configuration, and resolve the three PDF citation warnings through the required review process without a model signature. The GPL-3.0 pin and reviewed_by null are unchanged.
